newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey attacks European court ruling on Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Turkey attacks European court ruling on Cyprus.

text.p: Turkey on Thursday attacked as politically motivated a ruling by the European Court of Human Rights that Ankara had violated the rights of a Greek Cypriot with land in northern Cyprus.

"This decision has much more of a political character than a legal one because it is aimed at denying the existence of KKTC (the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus)," the Turkish Foreign Ministry said in a statement.

The breakaway state of northern Cyprus, declared in 1983, is only recognised by Ankara, which invaded the northern third of the island in 1974 after a coup there backed by the military regime then ruling Greece.

In a landmark finding, the Strasbourg court on Wednesday rejected Turkey's argument that the European human rights convention did not apply to its occupation of the north of Cyprus since it occurred before Ankara accepted the court's jurisdiction.
About 200,000 Greek Cypriots were displaced from the northern third in the 1974 invasion.

The court, an arm of the 40-nation Council of Europe that promotes human rights and democracy, upheld a complaint by tourist guide Titina Loizidou that Turkey violated her property rights by denying her access to land she owned in Kyrenia, northern Cyprus.
It found by a vote of 11-6 that the Turkish army "exercised effective overall control" in Cyprus. Turkey has some 30,000 troops stationed in northern Cyprus.
A statement from Turkish Cypriot administration said the court's decision threatened to harm international efforts to find a solution to the Cyprus problem.
